g.text: one shared bus on GPIO5/6 - STEMMA QT, in physical routing order
everything that is not on the I2C bus
TOUCH4 - BOTH shoulder pads, one net
TOUCH2 - free, to split the pads later
one 5 V / 5 A rail off the UPS
budget ~3.7 A of 5 A (crescent hard-capped at 65% white in firmware)
CHAIN KEY - balloons on WHERE THEY SIT
DS3231 RTC 0x68 rear wall, by the Flex
TPA2016 amp 0x58 rear wall, above the UPS
BH1750 lux 0x23 rear wall, light pipe
seesaw encoder 0x36 crown, under the knob
VL53L0X ToF 0x29 crown, right of the knob
NOTES (all from HARDWARE.md - that file is authoritative)
a ONE shared I2C bus on GPIO5/D4 (SDA) and GPIO6/D5 (SCL). D4/D5 is the tested mapping - do NOT 'correct' it from the schematic.
b BUS RUNS AT 100 kHz WITH A 1 ms TIMEOUT, deliberately. The STEMMA chain's cable capacitance and pull-ups were starving the
timing-sensitive XVF3800; the slow edges tolerate it and the timeout lets the XVF3800 clock-stretch while its firmware boots.
Chain order on this sheet is chosen to keep the cable SHORT for that reason. If it is still flaky, drop toward 10 kHz.
c BRIDGE-TIED AMP OUTPUTS. Every TPA2016 output terminal swings; there is no output ground. Do NOT common the two speakers'
negative leads and do NOT tie any output to GND - either shorts half a bridge and can kill the amp.
d The TPA2016's AGC is deliberately OFF (compression 1:1). An active compressor downstream of the DAC makes the echo path
time-varying and breaks the XVF3800's AEC. It has no NVM, so the custom component rewrites its config at every boot.
e The second matrix needs its ADDR jumper moved off 0x74 (0x75 / 0x76 / 0x77) and matrix_address_2 set to match.
f VL53L0X is drawn hidden: it is on the bus plan and in the address map but has NO ESPHome entity yet.
g INA219 address 0x41 is a PLACEHOLDER. Waveshare boards usually sit at 0x40-0x43; confirm against the boot I2C scan, and if the
readings are nonsense the part may be an INA226 (swap the platform in packages/battery.yaml).
h BOTH TOUCH PADS SHARE GPIO4/D3. Self-capacitance sensing measures the whole electrode net, so two pads on one net behave as
one electrode split in two - touching either half gives the same delta. One binary sensor, one threshold, no OR logic.
JOIN THE LEADS AT THE MCU, NOT ACROSS THE CROWN. Each lead drops down the inside of its own flank to the floor and they meet
at the XIAO. Same wire count either way, and it keeps a ~200 mm antenna out of the crown, where the SK6812 data line, the
I2S lines and the STEMMA chain all run. A wire taken straight across the crown would pick that up straight into the sensor.
Cost of sharing: baseline capacitance roughly doubles while the finger delta does not, so relative sensitivity drops (still
usable), and a side-to-side mismatch cannot be trimmed with per-pad thresholds. GPIO2/D1 (TOUCH2) is kept free as the escape
hatch - splitting to two channels is one wire at the MCU plus a few lines of YAML. Calibrate with esp32_touch: setup_mode: true.
i HT16K33 7-seg is the OPTIONAL alternative to the matrix. If you fit it, give it a dedicated 3.3 V LDO off the 5 V rail -
not the XIAO's 3V3 pin - and load the display package instead of matrix, never both.
one I2C bus, 100 kHz, 1 ms timeout
REFERENCE ONLY - not a released drawing
